saints.name: St. Romanus of Condat
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: A hermit of the Jura mountains whose solitude drew disciples and grew into the great monasteries of the region…
biography: Born about the year 400, Romanus withdrew at the age of thirty-five into the wild Jura mountains to live as a hermit, taking shelter beneath the firs of Condat. His younger brother Lupicinus followed him, and disciples gathered, among them the boy Eugendus, until the hermitage grew into a congregation of monks.

From it rose a family of houses: the abbey of Condat, around which grew the town now called Saint-Claude; Lauconne, later Saint-Lupicin, where Lupicinus was buried; the convent of La Balme for nuns, where Romanus himself was laid; and Romainmotier in what is now Switzerland.

Ordained priest by St. Hilary of Arles in 444, Romanus governed with a mildness that tempered the sterner temper of Lupicinus, and he was remembered for his tenderness toward lepers and the outcast. He died about 463; St. Gregory of Tours wrote his life in his Book of the Fathers.
saints.knownFor: Founding the monasteries of the Jura, among them Condat.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 28 February
